name: nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_4b_32
prose: Precondition: the caller is inside a kernel FPU section with AVX2 register ymm15 zeroed; f is a valid field whose lt lookup table, mt mapping table and bsize describe the bitmaps; map and fill are writable bitmaps of at least f->bsize longs; pkt points to at least 16 readable bytes; offset is non-negative. Postcondition: the function scans each 256-bit block i in [offset, f->bsize / NFT_PIPAPO_LONGS_PER_M256). When first is false and the map block is all zero, it skips the block and leaves it unchanged. When the AND of the 32 nibble buckets (with the map block, if first is false) is zero, it stores zero into the map block. Otherwise it stores the match bitmap into the map block and calls nft_pipapo_avx2_refill on it. If last is false, that call fills fill from the mapping table and clears the matched map bits. If last is true, it neither touches fill nor clears map. The function returns -1 if no block matched, which includes the case where the range is empty. If last is true it returns the bit index (rule index) of the lowest set bit in the highest-indexed matching block. Otherwise it returns the refill result of the first matching block, which is the mapping target of its lowest set bit, divided by XSAVE_YMM_SIZE. Nothing is allocated or freed.
note: In this version, last does not return early, so later matching blocks overwrite ret. [opus-5-5]

name: carl9170_interpolate_u8
prose: Precondition: x1, x2, y1, y2 and x are 0..255, x lies between x1 and x2 inclusive (in either order), and -32768 <= (y2-y1)*(x-x1) <= 32767, so that the 65536-scaled product inside carl9170_interpolate_s32 fits in 32 bits. Postcondition: if x2 == x1 it returns y1; otherwise let q = (256*(y2-y1)*(x-x1))/(x2-x1) with C division truncating toward zero, and it returns floor((256*y1 + q + 128)/256), which is a fixed-point interpolation truncated toward zero at 1/256 precision and then rounded half-up (for negative slopes this can differ from rounding the exact real interpolation), and the result is always in 0..255; it touches no memory, references or locks.
note: The prose now states the exact truncate-then-round computation instead of rounding the real-valued interpolation, and the ensures clauses are merged into one; the early returns for y2 == y1, x == x1 and x == x2 match the formula. [opus-5-5]

name: mei_cl_irq_read
prose: Precondition: cl is a valid client with a valid cl->dev, cb is a valid callback block linked on some list, and cmpl_list is a valid list head (the caller runs in the interrupt-thread context holding the device lock as usual for this path). Postcondition: if cl->rd_pending is non-empty it returns 0 without touching cb or cl->status; otherwise, if the host buffer empty-slot count is negative it returns -EOVERFLOW, and if it is smaller than the slots needed for a struct hbm_flow_control it returns -EMSGSIZE, in both cases without moving cb or changing cl->status; otherwise it sends a flow-control request, and if mei_hbm_cl_flow_control_req returns a nonzero error it sets cl->status to that error, sets cb->buf_idx to 0, moves cb to the tail of cmpl_list and returns that error; on success it marks dev->parent last-busy, requests its runtime autosuspend, moves cb to the tail of cl->rd_pending and returns 0; no locks or references are acquired or released.
note: Pointer parameters, so no formal contract; prose covers all four return paths. [opus-5-5]

name: hdr_is_valid
prose: Precondition: none; msg_hdr may be any 32-bit value, read through the struct mei_msg_hdr bitfield layout (little-endian: length in bits 16-24, reserved in bits 25-27, extended in bit 28, dma_ring in bit 29). Postcondition: it returns 0 exactly when msg_hdr is nonzero, its reserved field is zero, and its length field is at least 4 (MEI_SLOT_SIZE) times the number of set flags among dma_ring and extended; in every other case it returns -EBADMSG (-74); it has no side effects.
note: Corrected bit positions to the layout length:9, reserved:3, extended:1, dma_ring:1 and made the -EBADMSG (-74) result explicit. [opus-5-5]

name: instr_dw
prose: Precondition: cmd_header is any 32-bit instruction header value; the function reads no other state. Postcondition: it returns 1 when bits 31:27 (command type and GFXPIPE pipeline) equal those of GFXPIPE_SINGLE_DW_CMD(0,0), that is (cmd_header & 0xf8000000) == 0x68000000; otherwise, when bits 31:16 match CMD_3DSTATE_SO_DECL_LIST ((cmd_header & 0xffff0000) == 0x79170000), it returns the 9-bit length field in bits 8:0 plus 2; in every other case it returns the 8-bit length field in bits 7:0 plus 2; it takes or releases no locks, references or memory.
note: Masks recomputed from the xe headers: XE_INSTR_CMD_TYPE=GENMASK(31,29), GFXPIPE_PIPELINE=GENMASK(28,27), MATCH_MASK=GENMASK(31,16), SO_DECL_LIST DW_LEN=GENMASK(8,0). [opus-5-5]

name: htonll
prose: Precondition: none; this inline definition is compiled only for little-endian, non-LP64, non-_STANDALONE builds, and n may be any 64-bit unsigned value. Postcondition: the function returns htonl applied to the low 32 bits of n, shifted into the high 32 bits, plus htonl applied to the high 32 bits of n, which is n with its 8 bytes in reverse order; it has no side effects, allocates no memory and takes no locks.
note: The formal contract is left empty because the checker treats the uint64_t values as signed 64-bit integers, so the unsigned byte-swap formula is false for negative n and cannot be stated reliably. [opus-5-5]

name: hdmi_bus_fmt_is_rgb
prose: Precondition: none; bus_format may be any unsigned int value. Postcondition: returns true exactly when bus_format is MEDIA_BUS_FMT_RGB888_1X24 (0x100a), MEDIA_BUS_FMT_RGB101010_1X30 (0x1018), MEDIA_BUS_FMT_RGB121212_1X36 (0x1019) or MEDIA_BUS_FMT_RGB161616_1X48 (0x101a), and false for every other value.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures result == (bus_format == 0x100a || bus_format == 0x1018 || bus_format == 0x1019 || bus_format == 0x101a); */
note: Constants corrected to the media-bus-format.h values: RGB101010_1X30=0x1018, RGB121212_1X36=0x1019, RGB161616_1X48=0x101a. [opus-5-5]

name: hdmi_bus_fmt_is_yuv422
prose: Precondition: none; bus_format may be any unsigned int value. Postcondition: returns true exactly when bus_format is MEDIA_BUS_FMT_UYVY8_1X16 (0x200f), MEDIA_BUS_FMT_UYVY10_1X20 (0x201a) or MEDIA_BUS_FMT_UYVY12_1X24 (0x2020), and false for every other value.
note: Constants corrected to the media-bus-format.h values: UYVY10_1X20=0x201a, UYVY12_1X24=0x2020. [opus-5-5]

name: can_swapin_thp
prose: Precondition: nr_pages is a power of two greater than zero, vmf->orig_pte is the swap PTE that faulted at vmf->address, and ptep points to the first PTE slot of the nr_pages-aligned range containing vmf->address, inside a page table the caller has mapped and locked. Postcondition: returns true only if all four checks pass: (1) the PTE at ptep equals vmf->orig_pte with its swap offset moved back by idx, where idx is the faulting page's index within the aligned range; (2) swap_pte_batch reports that all nr_pages PTEs starting at ptep form one contiguous batch of swap entries; (3) all nr_pages swap entries have the same zeromap state; (4) none of the nr_pages swap entries has a swap-cache (SWAP_HAS_CACHE) entry; if any check fails it returns false, and in every case it takes and releases no lock and acquires no page or folio reference.
note: ptep is the first PTE of the aligned range, as the caller passes pte + pte_index(ALIGN_DOWN(address, PAGE_SIZE << order)); non_swapcache_batch requires that no entry is in the swap cache, not just that they all agree. [opus-5-5]

name: thp_swap_suitable_orders
prose: Precondition: orders is a bitmask of candidate THP orders whose highest set bit is at most 30, so the int shift 1 << order cannot overflow; swp_offset is the faulting entry's swap offset and addr is the faulting address. Postcondition: if no set order o in orders satisfies (addr >> PAGE_SHIFT) % (1 << o) == swp_offset % (1 << o), it returns 0; otherwise let o_max be the highest set order that satisfies it, and it returns orders with every bit above o_max cleared, so o_max is the highest set bit of the result; because congruence modulo 2^o_max implies congruence modulo every smaller power of two, every set bit of the result satisfies the congruence; the function has no side effects.
note: No formal contract: the ensures would need the PAGE_SHIFT macro, which the contract language does not allow, so the prose states the result exactly. [opus-5-5]

name: lzma_stream_encoder_mt_memusage
prose: Precondition: options is NULL or points to an lzma_mt structure that get_options() can read, and the products options->threads * block_size and filters_memusage * options->threads are not checked for overflow, so they are assumed to fit in uint64_t (get_options() limits threads and block_size). Postcondition: the function returns UINT64_MAX when get_options() does not return LZMA_OK (for example NULL or invalid options), when lzma_raw_encoder_memusage(filters) returns UINT64_MAX, when lzma_outq_memusage(outbuf_size_max, threads) returns UINT64_MAX, or when adding the input-buffer, filter and output-queue usages to the base LZMA_MEMUSAGE_BASE + sizeof(lzma_stream_coder) + threads * sizeof(worker_thread) would exceed UINT64_MAX; otherwise it returns that exact sum, and it acquires or releases no locks, references or heap memory.
note: The slice is the tail of lzma_stream_encoder_mt_memusage; it takes a pointer parameter, so there is no formal contract. [opus-5-5]

name: xtensa_pmu_cache_event
prose: Precondition: config is any 64-bit perf cache configuration value; its low byte is read as the cache type, its second byte as the cache op and its third byte as the cache result. Postcondition: the function returns -EINVAL (-22) when the type byte is greater than 4 (the table has 5 rows: L1D=0, L1I=1, LL=2, DTLB=3, ITLB=4), the op byte is greater than 2, the result byte is greater than 1, or the selected table entry is zero (type 0 with op 2, types 1, 3 and 4 with an op other than 0, and type 2 with any op); otherwise it returns the positive PMU control word stored in that entry (0x10AF1/0x20AF1 for L1D read, 0x10BF1/0x20BF1 for L1D write, 0x108F1/0x208F1 for L1I read, 0x109F1/0x809F1 for DTLB read, 0x107F1/0x807F1 for ITLB read, access/miss respectively), and it takes no locks and allocates no memory.
note: The table has 5 rows (index LL=2 is all zero, ITLB=4 is populated), so the old claim of 4 rows was wrong; the contract now gives the exact result including -EINVAL on every path. [opus-5-5]

name: gsmi_shutdown_reason
prose: Precondition: reason is a bit index from 0 to 30 inclusive, so that 1 << reason does not overflow an int, and gsmi_dev's lock, param_buf and data_buf are initialized. Postcondition: if bit reason is already set in the static saved_reason, the function returns 0 and does nothing else; otherwise it takes gsmi_dev.lock with interrupts saved, sets that bit (before the SMI call, so a failed attempt is not retried later), zeroes the data and parameter buffers, copies a kernel log entry carrying instance = reason into the data buffer and the set-event-log parameters into the parameter buffer, calls gsmi_exec(GSMI_CALLBACK, GSMI_CMD_SET_EVENT_LOG), and releases the lock; it then prints an error message if the result is negative and an emergency message otherwise, and returns gsmi_exec's return value unchanged.
note: gsmi_exec's return value is not constrained here (it can be positive), so the old ensures result <= 0 is not justified; the formal contract is omitted because the result depends on firmware and on static state. [opus-5-5]

name: local_hash_64
prose: Precondition: val is an unsigned 64-bit value and bits is between 1 and 64 inclusive. Postcondition: the function returns the top bits bits of val multiplied modulo 2^64 by 0x9E37FFFFFFFC0001 (the shift-and-add sequence computes exactly this product), which is a value less than 2^bits.
contract: /*@ requires 0 <= val && val <= 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF && 0 < bits && bits <= 64; ensures result == (((val * 0x9E37FFFFFFFC0001) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) >> (64 - bits)); */
note: The shifts implement multiplication by GOLDEN_RATIO_PRIME_64 0x9E37FFFFFFFC0001, not 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15, and val must be bounded as an unsigned value. [opus-5-5]

name: wpa_driver_ndis_get_names
prose: Precondition: drv points to an initialized NDIS driver context whose ifname holds a NUL-terminated interface name or description prefix to look for (with CONFIG_USE_NDISUIO, drv->ndisuio is an open NDISUIO handle); the caller keeps ownership of drv. Postcondition: once a matching adapter is found (a name containing ifname, or a description starting with ifname), drv->ifname may be rewritten to that adapter's device name with the "\DEVICE\" or "\Device\NPF_" prefix stripped, and on WinCE drv->adapter_name is set to a newly allocated copy; drv->adapter_desc is then overwritten, without freeing any old value, by a newly heap-allocated NUL-terminated description prefix (or NULL if that allocation fails), and the function returns 0 if that allocation succeeded; it returns -1 in every other case: the query buffer cannot be allocated, PacketGetAdapterNames fails, the adapter list is truncated or holds 32 or more names or descriptions, the name and description counts differ, no adapter matches (including when the NDISUIO query ioctl fails), the WinCE adapter_name allocation fails, or the adapter_desc allocation fails (drv->adapter_desc is then NULL, while any ifname rewrite and the WinCE adapter_name allocation already done stay in place); the temporary query/name buffer is freed on every path that allocated it.
note: The slice is part of wpa_driver_ndis_get_names, so the whole function is annotated; the old prose wrongly claimed adapter_name stays NULL or unchanged on failure. [opus-5-5]

name: nfs4_stat_to_errno
prose: Precondition: stat may be any int NFSv4 status code; the function takes no lock, reference or memory. Postcondition: it returns the errno paired with stat in nfs4_errtbl_common, which is checked first (0→0, 1→-1, 2→-2, 5→-5, 6→-6, 13→-13, 17→-17, 18→-18, 20→-20, 21→-21, 22→-22, 27→-27, 28→-28, 30→-30, 31→-31, 63→-36, 66→-39, 69→-122, 70→-116, 10001→-521, 10003→-523, 10004→-524, 10005→-525, 10007→-527, 10029→-40, 10045→-35), otherwise the errno paired with stat in nfs4_errtbl (10006→-121, 10012→-11, 10044→-95, 10095→-61, 10096→-7); if neither table matches, it returns -EREMOTEIO (-121) when stat <= 10000 or stat > 10100, and -stat when 10000 < stat <= 10100.

name: get_omac_idx
prose: Precondition: none beyond mask being the driver's current 64-bit omac allocation bitmask; type may be any nl80211_iftype value, and the only side effect is a WARN_ON(1) when type is not station, adhoc, mesh point, monitor or AP. Postcondition: for NL80211_IFTYPE_STATION it returns the lowest index in HW_BSSID_1..HW_BSSID_3 whose bit is clear in mask, else the lowest clear bit in REPEATER_BSSID_START..REPEATER_BSSID_MAX given at its absolute index (32..63), else the lowest clear bit in EXT_BSSID_1..EXT_BSSID_MAX, else HW_BSSID_0 if its bit is clear, else -1; for NL80211_IFTYPE_ADHOC, MESH_POINT, MONITOR and AP it returns HW_BSSID_0 if its bit is clear, else the lowest clear bit in EXT_BSSID_1..EXT_BSSID_MAX, else -1; for any other type it triggers WARN_ON(1) and returns -1; any non-negative result is an index whose bit is clear in mask.
note: Removed the false 'pure/no side effects' claim; the formal contract is left empty because the full lowest-free-bit preference order cannot be stated cleanly in the allowed contract language. [opus-5-5]

name: mul_u64_u64_div_u64
prose: Precondition: z is nonzero and the exact quotient fits in 64 bits, i.e. the mathematical product x * y is less than 2^64 * z (if z is 0 the division y / z is undefined, and if the quotient does not fit, res wraps modulo 2^64). Postcondition: the function returns floor(x * y / z), computed exactly over the full 128-bit product by shift-and-add with remainder rem < z, so both KASSERTs hold; it has no side effects and touches no memory, locks or references.
note: The formal contract was removed because the precondition needs constants such as 2^64 * z that overflow when evaluated in 64-bit machine arithmetic, which made random testing report false failures; the prose states the exact condition. [opus-5-5]

name: mul_u64_u32_shr
prose: Precondition: shift is at most 32, so both shifts are by 0..32 bits of a 64-bit value, and the mathematical value (x * y) >> shift is less than 2^64, so the left-shifted high partial product and the sum do not wrap. Postcondition: the function returns exactly floor(x * y / 2^shift), computed as ((low 32 bits of x) * y >> shift) + ((high 32 bits of x) * y << (32 - shift)); it has no side effects and touches no memory, locks or references.
contract: /*@ requires shift <= 32 && ((x * y) >> shift) < 18446744073709551616; ensures result == ((x * y) >> shift); */
note: shift == 0 and shift == 32 are both valid because the shifted operands are 64-bit, and the split is exact because hi*y*2^(32-shift) is an integer. [opus-5-5]

name: __serial_get_clock_div
prose: Precondition: rate is nonzero and uartclk is less than 2^32, so div = uartclk/rate fits in the u32 variable. Postcondition: if uartclk/rate < 14 the u32 computation (div/14)-1 wraps, the tuning loop does not run, and the function returns 4294967295. Otherwise, with k = (uartclk/rate)/14, it tries the candidates 0, 1, 2 when k == 1, or k-2, k-1, k when k >= 2. It returns the candidate h whose uartclk/((h+1)*14) is closest to rate, taking the earliest candidate on ties. It takes no locks, has no side effects and allocates or frees no memory.
contract: /*@ requires rate > 0 && uartclk < 4294967296; ensures ((uartclk / rate) < 14 ==> result == 4294967295) && (((uartclk / rate) >= 14 && (uartclk / rate) < 28) ==> result <= 2) && ((uartclk / rate) >= 28 ==> (result <= (uartclk / rate) / 14 && result + 2 >= (uartclk / rate) / 14)); */
note: Bounds are tightened to the exact candidate windows: 0..2 when k == 1 and k-2..k when k >= 2; the closest-match selection is stated only in the prose. [opus-5-5]

name: wpa_cipher_to_alg
prose: Precondition: none; cipher is compared for exact equality against single WPA_CIPHER_* constants, so a value that combines several bits matches no case. Postcondition: the function returns WPA_ALG_CCMP_256 for WPA_CIPHER_CCMP_256, WPA_ALG_GCMP_256 for WPA_CIPHER_GCMP_256, WPA_ALG_CCMP for WPA_CIPHER_CCMP, WPA_ALG_GCMP for WPA_CIPHER_GCMP, WPA_ALG_TKIP for WPA_CIPHER_TKIP, WPA_ALG_BIP_CMAC_128 for WPA_CIPHER_AES_128_CMAC, WPA_ALG_BIP_GMAC_128 for WPA_CIPHER_BIP_GMAC_128, WPA_ALG_BIP_GMAC_256 for WPA_CIPHER_BIP_GMAC_256 and WPA_ALG_BIP_CMAC_256 for WPA_CIPHER_BIP_CMAC_256, and WPA_ALG_NONE for every other value; it touches no locks, references or memory.
note: Formal contract omitted because the numeric values of the WPA_CIPHER_* macros and wpa_alg enumerators are defined outside this file and could not be confirmed. [opus-5-5]

name: wpa_cipher_to_suite
prose: Precondition: none; cipher is treated as a bitmask of WPA_CIPHER_* bits, and proto only decides between RSN and WPA selectors for CCMP, TKIP and NONE. Postcondition: the function returns the selector for the first set bit in this order: WPA_CIPHER_CCMP_256 gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_CCMP_256; WPA_CIPHER_GCMP_256 gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_GCMP_256; WPA_CIPHER_CCMP gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_CCMP if proto == WPA_PROTO_RSN, otherwise WPA_CIPHER_SUITE_CCMP; WPA_CIPHER_GCMP gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_GCMP; WPA_CIPHER_TKIP gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_TKIP if proto == WPA_PROTO_RSN, otherwise WPA_CIPHER_SUITE_TKIP; WPA_CIPHER_NONE gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_NONE if proto == WPA_PROTO_RSN, otherwise WPA_CIPHER_SUITE_NONE; WPA_CIPHER_GTK_NOT_USED gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_NO_GROUP_ADDRESSED; WPA_CIPHER_AES_128_CMAC gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_AES_128_CMAC; WPA_CIPHER_BIP_GMAC_128 gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_BIP_GMAC_128; WPA_CIPHER_BIP_GMAC_256 gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_BIP_GMAC_256; WPA_CIPHER_BIP_CMAC_256 gives RSN_CIPHER_SUITE_BIP_CMAC_256. It returns 0 when none of these bits is set, and it touches no locks, references or memory.
note: Formal contract omitted because the numeric values of the WPA_CIPHER_*, WPA_PROTO_RSN and suite macros are defined outside this file and could not be confirmed. [opus-5-5]

name: __fixunsdfdi
prose: Precondition: x is not NaN (for NaN no early return fires and the double-to-unsigned-long conversions are undefined), and long is 32 bits wide so that ONE is 2^32 and the union uu halves are 32-bit words. Postcondition: if x < 0, or x >= 18446744073709551615.0 (a constant that rounds to 2^64, so in effect x >= 2^64), the function returns UQUAD_MAX; otherwise it returns trunc(x) + 1 when x > 2^32 - 1 and (x mod 2^32) is either greater than 2^32 - 1 or less than 2^31 (for example x = 2^32 gives 2^32 + 1), and exactly trunc(x) in all other cases; the off-by-one comes from the correction step subtracting ULONG_MAX instead of 2^32, and the function acquires or releases no locks, references or memory.
note: The second reviewer is right that the correction step subtracts ULONG_MAX instead of 2^32, so the prose now states exactly when the result is trunc(x)+1; the parameter is a double, so no formal contract is given. [opus-5-5]

name: inet_network
prose: Precondition: cp points to a readable NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: the string is parsed as dot-separated parts, each written as an optional leading '0' (selects octal and counts as a digit) followed by an optional 'x' or 'X' (selects hex, even without the leading 0) and then digits (hex parts accept 0-9, a-f and A-F; decimal and octal parts stop at the first non-digit), with val*base and val<<4 wrapping silently in in_addr_t; the result is INADDR_NONE if a part has no digit at all (so the empty string, a leading space, a lone "x" or a trailing or doubled '.' fail, while "0" and a bare "0x" are the value 0), if an '8' or '9' appears in an octal part, if a part's wrapped value exceeds 0xff, if a fifth part is reached, or if the last part is followed by a character that is neither NUL nor whitespace; otherwise, with n (1 to 4) parts p[0..n-1], the result is p[0]<<8*(n-1) | ... | p[n-1], i.e. the parts packed big-endian into the low n bytes (for example "1.2" gives 0x0102), and everything after a whitespace terminator is ignored and never read; the function allocates, frees and locks nothing.
note: Prose corrected: bare "0x" yields 0, a part may start with 'x' alone, and the parts fill only the low n bytes; no formal contract because the parameter is a pointer. [opus-5-5]

name: vt_parse_rgb_triplet
prose: Precondition: rgb points to a NUL-terminated string and r, g and b each point to one writable unsigned char. Postcondition: the function returns 0 in exactly two cases, and returns -1 for every other input: (a) the first character is '#', strlen of the whole string is exactly 7, and base-16 strtoul applied to the six characters after '#' consumes all of them; strtoul also accepts leading whitespace, a '+' or '-' sign (a '-' wraps the value) and a 0x prefix within those six characters, so a seven-character string such as "#0x1234", "#+12345", "# 12345" or "#-10000" also succeeds, and *r, *g and *b receive bits 16-23, 8-15 and 0-7 of the resulting unsigned long; (b) otherwise, the string is consumed by three successive base-10 strtoul conversions, each converting at least one digit and each yielding a value of at most 255, in which case *r, *g and *b receive the three values; strtoul skips leading whitespace and an optional sign before each number, and a '-' sign wraps, so only "-0" passes; between conversions any run, possibly empty, of ',' and ' ' characters is skipped; after the last number only ' ' characters may follow. In case (a) a -1 return leaves *r, *g and *b unchanged, while in case (b) a -1 return may leave *r, or *r and *g, already set from components parsed earlier; the function allocates and frees no memory.
note: Takes pointer parameters, so there is no formal contract; the earlier wrong example "# 1234" (strlen 6) is replaced by the seven-character "# 12345". [opus-5-5]
